final_recommendation: The room converged on a comprehensive trilateral package: 75% auto RVC with 24-month phase-in, plant-level labor value content measurement with quarterly audits and automatic tariff suspension (90-day one-time grace period), Mexico certifying independent unions by Q1 2019 before signature, ten-year agreement with year-seven review trigger (not sunset), and Canada's Chapter 19 and dairy supply management preserved as red lines. USTR committed to draft binding text immediately with Friday initialing contingent on Canada committing a dairy quota number simultaneously.
minority_objections: Dairy sector demanded meaningful Canadian market access quota increase as the price for the deal, creating final pressure on Canada
Supply-chain manufacturers raised ongoing uncertainty about quarterly audit mechanics and recertification windows
key_conflicts: Canada's absolute red line on Chapter 19 dispute settlement and dairy supply management versus U.S. pressure for dairy market access
Labor union demand for immediate automatic tariff suspension versus auto industry need for 90-day operational grace period
Business demand for investment certainty (no sunset) versus initial U.S. preference for six-year sunset clause
key_concessions: USTR abandoned six-year sunset in favor of ten-year floor with year-seven review trigger
USTR took Chapter 19 and dairy completely off the table as negotiating leverage
Canada accepted 75% RVC and enforceable labor value content with automatic sanctions
Auto industry accepted quarterly audits with automatic suspension after one-time 90-day grace
Mexico committed to Q1 2019 independent union certification before agreement takes effect
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement mechanism non-negotiable
Canada: Dairy supply management off the table entirely
Labor unions: Automatic tariff suspension on backsliding, no USTR discretion to waive
Auto industry: No hard sunset that creates investment uncertainty
Congress: Mexico must certify labor reforms before signature, not after
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Actual dairy quota number Canada would commit remained unspecified despite being critical to final signature
Operational details of quarterly audit scope and supplier-tier measurement left partially undefined
Timeline risk: Friday initialing deadline with binding text drafted Wednesday-Thursday creates compression
Congressional ratification timeline and political calendar not explicitly addressed
downstream_risk_variables: Canada's domestic political capacity to deliver meaningful dairy quota increase
Mexico's ability to pass independent union reforms through Congress by Q1 2019
USTR's operational capacity to implement plant-level quarterly audits across three countries
Supply-chain compliance costs and timeline for 75% RVC recertification within 24-month phase-in
Congressional ratification vote timing and Democratic/Republican coalition dynamics
uncertainty_notes: The specific dairy quota number Canada would commit remained unresolved at meeting end, creating signature risk. The precise operational mechanics of quarterly labor audits (supplier-tier scope, data verification process, sanction implementation timeline) were outlined in principle but not fully specified. The year-seven review trigger mechanism's political dynamics (who initiates, what threshold to terminate) were clarified as continuation-unless-killed but procedural details unstated.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and labor value content drove the entire negotiation structure; plant-level measurement and quarterly audits were the core enforcement mechanism that unlocked the package
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Automatic tariff suspension with no USTR discretion was the explicit condition for labor union ratification support and drove Mexico's Q1 2019 certification requirement
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy was raised repeatedly as pressure point but USTR ultimately took it off the table; it remained unresolved as quota number but did not block the package formation
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 was non-negotiable multiple times and USTR explicitly agreed to take it off the table permanently as condition for Canada signing
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Auto industry and supply-chain manufacturers rejected six-year sunset as investment killer; USTR shifted to ten-year floor with year-seven review trigger as the compromise that closed the deal
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress raised enforcement sequencing and labor union support as constraints, but these were addressed within the negotiation; ratification was a background concern, not a deal-shaping force
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain manufacturers raised compliance costs and recertification windows as concerns requiring the 90-day grace period, but this was accommodated rather than blocking progress
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico and USTR explicitly threatened bilateral-only deal multiple times to pressure Canada on dairy and timeline; this was the primary leverage forcing Canada to commit to Friday initialing
